Payal: (30 years old, normal) It's good that we took out all the winter clothes from the bed and trunk today and washed them properly.  The cold weather has just started. Later, when it gets colder, it will be very difficult to wash clothes in cold water.

Neha: (28 years old, normal) You're absolutely right, Didi. The weather is nice today, there's even a little sunshine.  It's true that the cold has started, but it's not too much of a problem yet. When it gets really cold, it will be much more difficult to wash clothes and do other chores involving water.

Narrator: Both of them wash the winter clothes and hang them on the roof to dry. After that, they come down to the courtyard and water their plants and crops.

Payal: (30 years old, worried) Oh, whenever I look at the rest of my garden, seeing the beautiful flowers makes me happy. But as soon as I come near this part, my mind goes completely crazy.

Neha: (28 years old, normal) This is nothing, Didi, this is just the beginning. Just wait and see what happens next.

Payal: (30 years old, normal) You're absolutely right, the whole game is yet to unfold. Let's make lunch, it's almost lunchtime.

Narrator: Both of them go inside the house. They were just going towards the kitchen when their mother-in-law, Shanti, stops them and says:

Shanti: (55 years old, normal) Hey daughters-in-law, make some food, I'm very hungry.

Payal: (30 years old, normal) Yes, Mummy ji, we were just about to make food.

Shanti: (55 years old, normal) Okay, but what are you going to make for food?

Neha: (28 years old, normal) We were thinking of making matar paneer (peas and cottage cheese curry), Mummy ji.

Shanti: (55 years old, normal) Oh, forget matar paneer, what's so special about it? You both do one thing, make a nice potato and cauliflower curry today, it will be delicious!  Payal: (30 years old, normal) But Mom, the cauliflower hasn't even started growing in the courtyard yet. So where will we get cauliflower from? There's still time. The winter is still mild, so we can eat other vegetables for now.

Shanti: (55 years old, normal) Never mind, that's why I told you a long time ago to sow the seeds, but no, both of you are too lazy to work. Now you know, we eat potato and cauliflower curry every winter, nothing else. Do one thing, make some poha for me for now. I'll eat some peanuts too, that will satisfy my hunger, and go to the market and bring back potatoes and cauliflower today itself. Potato and cauliflower curry should start being made at home from today.

Narrator: Hearing this, a look of sadness spreads across Payal and Neha's faces.

Payal: (30 years old, normal) Okay Mom, we're going.

Narrator: The two of them first make poha for Shanti, and Shanti sits comfortably watching TV and enjoying the poha. Meanwhile, Payal and Neha leave for the market with a bag.

Payal: (30 years old, normal) I thought we had a few more days, and until the vegetables grow in the courtyard, we could eat other vegetables, but Mom has ordered us to eat potato and cauliflower from today itself.

Neha: (28 years old, angry) Honestly, Didi, I'm so angry too.  There's a limit to everything, who eats so much potato and cauliflower? Now, potato and cauliflower will be made every day in the winter. Our in-laws are the stingiest people ever. They want to grow cauliflower at home, and cauliflower is cheap, that's why only potato and cauliflower will be made. Huh.  They have so much money, what would happen if they spent a little money on vegetables?

Payal: (30 years old, normal) They measure and weigh everything; they don't let a single rupee go to waste.  We've really ended up in a very stingy family.  Narrator: They both go to the vegetable vendor and buy vegetables.

Payal: (30 years old, normal) Hey brother, please give me 5 kilos of cauliflower and 5 kilos of potatoes.

Vegetable Vendor: (45 years old, normal) Okay, sister.  Should I give you any other vegetables too?

Neha: (28 years old, normal) No, brother, we only cook potatoes and cauliflower in the winter, so just give us these.

Vegetable Vendor: (45 years old, normal) Oh madam, eat other vegetables too! There are so many other delicious vegetables in the world. Why are you stuck on just potatoes and cauliflower?

About Taarak Mehta Ka Ooltah Chashmah:
--------------------------------------------------------------------
The show is inspired from the famous humorous column 'Duniya Ne Undha Chasma' written by the eminent Gujarati writer Mr. Tarak Mehta. This story revolves around daily happenings in "Gokuldham Co-operative Society" and covers topical issues which are socially relevant. The show predominantly - revolves around 'Jethalal' who is an uneducated Gujarati businessman. Your 'Taarak Mehta', is his neighbor. 'Jethalal' finds a friend and philosopher in 'Taarak Mehta' and often goes to him for advice whenever he is in trouble. Jethalaal's family includes his simpleton wife 'Daya Ben' and a mischievous son 'Tapu'. Tapu is a menace and a constant source of trouble to all the members of Gokuldham. They have often warned 'Jethalal' to reform 'Tapu' or else be prepared to leave the premises. Lost hopes of being heard by his son push Jethalal' to call his father 'Champaklal' from the village. This was his great idea of leashing some control over the mischievous Tapu. The opposite happens and the grandfather joins hands with the grandson to make life a roller coaster troublesome ride for Jethalal.
